findings.title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty array and location is Google Meet
findings.body: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is an empty array `[]` (which is the default set in many code paths like `selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []`), the destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined`. The subsequent access `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. This crashes any booking flow where Google Meet is the location but no destination calendar is configured.

findings.title: Logic inversion: slug is now set when billing IS enabled, opposite of original intent
findings.body: The original code `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` included `slug` when billing was NOT enabled (so the org gets a slug immediately without needing to go through billing). The new code `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` includes `slug` when billing IS enabled, which is the opposite behavior. This means organizations will not get a slug when billing is disabled (breaking self-hosted instances) and will get a slug prematurely when billing is enabled (before payment is confirmed).

findings.title: Dead code in updateEvent fallback: find condition can never match when externalCalendarId is falsy
findings.body: In `updateEvent`, the fallback branch `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (empty string, null, undefined). Since it searches for a calendar where `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` and `externalCalendarId` is falsy, no calendar will ever match (externalId is always a non-empty string). The result is always `undefined`, making the fallback useless. The same issue exists in `deleteEvent` at line 317.

findings.title: updateEvent called with potentially undefined credential after DB lookup fails
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` and the DB lookup returns null or a credential without `app.slug`, the variable `credential` remains `undefined`. The code then calls `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId))` with `undefined` as the credential, which will cause a runtime error inside `updateEvent` when it tries to access properties of the credential.

findings.title: createAllCalendarEvents silently skips calendar creation when credential not found
findings.body: In `createAllCalendarEvents`, when a destination calendar has a `credentialId` but the credential cannot be found either in `this.calendarCredentials` or in the database (or the DB credential lacks an `app.slug`), the code silently skips creating the calendar event with no logging or error. For collective events with multiple hosts, this means a host's calendar event may silently fail to be created, leading to missed calendar entries without any indication of failure.

findings.title: Inconsistent destinationCalendar format in webhook payloads: null vs empty array
findings.body: The BOOKING_CREATED webhook test expects `destinationCalendar: null` (line 119) while BOOKING_REJECTED expects `destinationCalendar: []` (line 249). This inconsistency in the webhook payload format is a breaking change for webhook consumers who may be checking for `null` specifically. The BOOKING_CREATED path likely still serializes `destinationCalendar` as `null` when no calendar is set, while BOOKING_REJECTED now sends an empty array. A consistent format should be chosen.

findings.title: await on array does not wait for promises to resolve
findings.body: At line 619, `await apiDeletes` awaits an array of promises directly, which resolves immediately without waiting for the individual promises to settle. This should be `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` or `await Promise.allSettled(apiDeletes)`. As a result, the function may return success before calendar events are actually deleted from external providers. While this is a pre-existing issue, the surrounding code was significantly modified in this PR.
